reference.omp_note: OpenMP target-offload program for icpx, absent on the remote host; g++ -fopenmp host fallback only parallelises the innermost loop, so it is not a like-for-like CPU baseline

timing_scope: forward-elimination time only: one size-1 step elimination per sample, timed between two host synchronisations; matches the reference '-t' scope (fan1/fan2 loop). One warm-up elimination precedes the measured samples; median of 5 samples.
acceptance_metric: GPU (CUDA) runtime ratio, median alpaka / median reference

performance_exceptions.summary: Small-N launch-overhead exception above the 1.10 acceptance bound. At N=1024 the reference launches 2*(N-1)=2046 kernels, as does this port, but each kernel is tiny (<2M element updates total) so the measured interval is dominated by per-launch overhead; the CUDA runtime launch path is cheaper than alpaka's Queue::enqueue path for this short-kernel regime. The gap closes as work per kernel grows: N=2048 and N=4096 are 1.4-2.4x faster than the reference, so the port is not slower in the compute-bound regime.

The N=2048 reference median is noisy because the Quadro GV100 is a shared, non-exclusive machine: the reference's own five samples spanned 60.3-134.9 ms (median 134.6) while this port's spanned 47.0-55.2 ms (median 55.2). Treat the 0.410 ratio as indicative.

validation.kind: double-precision partial-pivot LU oracle (gaussianGoldDouble) plus a relative-residual check
validation.rationale: the reference itself accepts atol 1e-3 between its single-precision device run and its single-precision host reference. Our oracle is double precision with partial pivoting, so the difference is dominated by the benchmark's own rounding. Measured worst-case absolute differences stay below 1.8e-5, so atol=rtol=1e-3 leaves more than a 50x margin. The residual check is the stronger gate: for a correct solution it stays below 3e-6 at N=4096, while a wrong elimination pushes it toward O(1).
validation.result: PASS on host CPU and CUDA backends
